sections.description:
Interpretation

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
2. Interpretation.--In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant
in the subject or context,‑
(1) "Government" means,
in reference to offences this Act committed in British Balochistan
or the Capital of the Federation, the Central Government, and in reference to
such offences committed in a Governor's Province the Provincial Government;
(2) "dealing
in the black market" means-‑
(a) otherwise than in accordance with any Pakistan law‑
(i) selling, bartering, exchanging,
supplying, or disposing of articles rationed by or under any such law;
(ii) supplying,
distributing, selling, disposing of or parting with the possession or custody
of, or offering to supply, distribute, sell, batter exchange, dispose of or
part with the possession or custody of, or acquiring or taking into possession
anything, the supply, distribution, sale, barter, exchange, disposal, parting with
the possession or custody, acquiring or taking into possession of which is by
or under any such law prohibited or subject to any restrictions or conditions
whether of price of otherwise;
(iii) producing, manufacturing, or treating anything the production,
manufacture or treatment of which is subject to restriction or conditions
imposed by or under any such law;
(iv) moving or
purporting to sell, barter, exchange or supply or purporting to acquire or take
into possession for the purposes of trade anything vested in his Majesty by or
under any law for the time begin in force;
(v) using or dealing with any licence,
permit or ration document issued by or under any such law;
(b) marking,
uttering or using any counterfeit or forged licence,
permit or ration document purporting to be a licence,
permit or ration document duly granted or issued under any Pakistan law;
(c) in contravention of a prohibition, restriction or direction
imposed in that behalf by or under any Pakistan law;
(i) string or taking, causing,
permitting or suffering the delivering of anything upon any premises; or
(ii) withholding anything from sale; or
(d) selling or buying anything for purposes of trade at a price
greater than the maximum price fixed by or under any Pakistan law;
(3) "hoarding" means
stocking or storing anything in excess of the maximum quantity of that thing
allowed to be held in stock or storage at any one time by any person by or under
any Pakistan law; and
(4) "Special Judge"
means a person appointed as such under this Act.

Punishment for hoarding or dealing in black market

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
3. Punishment for hoarding or dealing in black market.--(1) Whoever
is found guilty of the offence of hoarding or dealing in the black market shall,
notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other enactment for the time
being in force, be punishable‑
(a) if the
offence is tried summarily, with imprisonment which may extend to one year but
shall not, except for reason to be recorded, be less than six months, and with
fine; and
(b) if the offence is not tried summarily, with imprisonment
which may extend to seven years but shall not, except for reason to be
recorded, be less than one year, and with fine:
Provided that if
in the case of an offence of hoarding, the person accused of such offence
proves that he was hoarding for purposes other than gain, whether financial or
otherwise, he shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six
months or with fine which extend to five thousand rupees or with both.
(2) A Court convicting any person
of an offence of hoarding or dealing in that black market shall order the
forfeiture to the Government of anything in respect of which the offence was
committed, or, where such forfeiture is impossible than forfeiture of an
equivalent quantity of the like thing belonging to such person, or may order
such person, notwithstanding any fine that may be imposed upon him under this
section, to forfeit the equivalent value in money of such thing assessed at the
date of the order of forfeiture.
sections.punishment:
punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six
months or with fine which extend to five thousand rupees or with both.

sections.description:
Short title extent and commencement

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
1. Short title extent and commencement.--(1) This Act may be called
the Hoarding and Black Market Act, 1948.
(2) It extends to all the
Provinces of Pakistan and to the Capital of the Federation.
(3) It shall come into force on
such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the official
Gazette, appoint.

Attempts and Abetments

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
6. Attempts and Abetments.--Any person who attempts to commit an
offence under this Act, or abets or attempts to abete
the commission of such an offence, shall be deemed to have committed that
offence.

Power of Government as to prosecution

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
12. Power of Government as to prosecution.--(1) No Court shall take cognizance of any
offence of hoarding or dealing in the black market except upon a complaint in
writing by or under the written authority of the Government.
(2) The Government may by order
direct that in case of trials other than trials before a Special Judge the
powers conferred upon it by sub-section (1) shall, in such circumstances and
under such conditions if any, as may be specified in the order, be exercised by
District Magistrate.

Power to try summarily

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
13. Power to try summarily.--Any Magistrate for the time being
empowered to try in a summary way the offences specified in sub-section (1) of
section 260 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, may, if he thinks application
in this behalf by the prosecution, and after in accordance of sub-section (1)
of section 262 and Sections 263, 264 and 265 of that Code.

Prohibition of carrying on business in certain cases

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
4. Prohibition of carrying on business in certain cases.--(1) On
the third of any subsequent occasion on which a person is convicted of an
offence under this Act the Government may make an order, having effect during
such period as it thinks fit to fix, forbidding the convicted person to carry
on or be concerned in any manner directly or indirectly with the carrying on
the business in the course of which the offence was committed, or any branch of
that business or any business or branch of a business of a similar character.
(2) Whoever contravenes an order
under this section shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description
for a term which may extend to six months and with fine.
sections.punishment:
punishable with imprisonment of either description
for a term which may extend to six months and with fine.

sections.description:
Vicarious liability

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
5. Vicarious liability.--(1) Where an
offence of hoarding or dealing in the black market is committed-‑
(a) by a body corporate, every director, manager, secretary or
other officer or servant, or
(b) by a firm, every partnership, secretary, principal officer
and every agent of the partnership, or
(c) by a joint Hindu Family business, the harta,
every adult member, manager, gomasta, agent or
servant‑
shall,
if actively concerned in the conduct of the bUsiness
of such body firm, or joint Hindu family, be deemed to have committed the
offence unless he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge
and that he used all diligence to prevent the commission of the offence.
(2) The provisions of section 12
shall apply to any offence referred to in sub--section (1) of this section,
(3) Where a harta,
adult member, manager, gomasta, agent or servant of a
joint Hindu family business is fined, the fine shall be realizable from his
personal property and also from the assets of the joint family.

Abetment by public servants

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
7. Abetment by public servants.--Any public servant as defined in
the Penal Code XLV of 1860 who by a dereliction of duty facilitates the
commission by any person of an offence of hoarding or dealing in the black
market, shall be deemed to have abetted the commission of the said offence
within the meaning of section 6.

Bond by convicted person

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
8. Bond by convicted person.--(1) The Court on convicting any
person under the Act may in addition to any punishment to bond for a sum
proportionate to his means, with or without sureties, to be of good behaviour for a period not exceeding three years.
(2) If he fails to execute the
bond on or before the date on which the period for which the bond is to be
given commences, the Court may order him to be committed to prison, or, if he
is already in prison, to be detained in prison, until he executed the bond, and
such detention shall if the punishment referred to in sub-section (1) includes
a term of imprisonment, commence at the expiration of that term of shall in no
case exceed twelve months.
(3) If having executed the bond
he commits any breach of any condition in bond, the bond shall forthwith stand
forfeited, and he, and in his default any other person bound by the bond as
security, shall pay the penalty thereof:
Provided that if
the person executing the bond shows cause to the satisfaction of the Court why
such penalty should not be levied from him it shall not be levied from him or
from any security to the bond.
(4) Imprisonment for failure to
execute the bond shall be simple.

Bond for goods behaviour in certain cases

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
9. Bond for goods behaviour in certain
cases.--Whenever a District Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class specially
empowered in this behalf, has information there is within the limits or his
jurisdiction any person who within
without such limits transports foodstuff in contravention of an order
made or deemed to have been made under the Essential Supplies (Temporary
Powers) Act, XXIV of 1946; he may, if in his opinion there is sufficient ground
for proceeding, require such person to show cause why he should not be ordered
to execute a bond with or without sureties for his good behaviour
for such period not exceeding one year as the Magistrate thinks fit to fix, and
upon the execution of such bond the provisions of Chapters VIII and XLII of the
Code of Criminal Procedure V of 1898 shall apply to the case.
(2) Any contravention of an order
made under the Essential Supplies (Temporary Powers) Act, XXIV of 1946,
committed by such person after the execution of such bond shall be deemed to
constitute a forfeiture of the bond.

Arrest and bail

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
10. Arrest and bail.--Any offence punishable under this Act shall
be cognizable and, except as provided in section 11 bail shall not be granted
for an offence punishable under this Act except in accordance with the
proceeding provided in sections 497 and
498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, for the grant of bail in case of
non-bailable offence.
sections.punishment:
punishable under this Act shall
be cognizable and, except as provided in section 11 bail shall not be granted
for an offence punishable under this Act except in accordance with the
proceeding provided in sections 497 and
498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, for the grant of bail in case of
non-bailable offence.

sections.description:
Special provision regarding bait

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
11. Special provision regarding bait--Notwithstanding anything
contained offence in the Code of Criminal Procedure, V of 1898, no person accused
of an under the Act in a trial before a
Special Judge for any such offence shall be released on bail or on his own bond
unless the prosecution has been given an opportunity to be heard in the matter.

Appointment of Special Judge

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
14. Appointment of Special Judge.--(1) The Central Government shall
have power to appoint Special Judges for the trial of offences under this Act.
(2) Any person may be appointed a
Special Judge who--
(a) is or has been a Judge of a High Court, or a Sessions Judge,
or
(b) is qualified to be appointed a Judge of the High Court.
(3) Every Special Judge shall be
appointed by the Central Government after consulting the High Court having
jurisdiction in the area for which the Special Judge is to be appointed:
Provided that
nothing in this sub-section shall be deemed to forbid the appointment of a
Special Judge for an area in which two or more High Courts have jurisdiction.

Cases triable by Special Judge

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
15. Cases triable by Special Judge.--(1)
Every Special Judge shall try such case under the Act as the Government may
from time to time appoint in this regard by notification in the official
Gazette, and notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other enactment
for the time being in force , any such case which at the date of a notification
under sub-section (2) is pending before any other Court shall on such date, be
deemed to stand transferred to the Special fudge concerned in accordance with
the notification.
(2) The Government may by a like
notification transfer any such case from one Special Judge, to another, or
withdraw any case from a Special Judge, or make such modification in the
description of any case (whether in the name of any accused or in the charge
preferred or in any other manner) as it may necessary.

Procedure and powers by Special Judges

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
16. Procedure and powers by Special Judges.--(A) Special Judge may
take cognizance of a case without the accused being committed for trial, and in
trying the case he shall follow the procedure prescribed by the Code of
Criminal Procedure, V of 1898 for the trial of warrant cases by Magistrates:
Provided that a
Special Judge shall not be bound to adjourn any trial for any purpose whatever,
unless such adjournment is in his opinion necessary in the interests of
justice.
Provided further
that notwithstanding anything in the aforesaid Code Special Judge may, unless
he in his discretion otherwise decides and except where a case has been
transferred to him by the High Court on the ground that fair and impartial
Trial Court not be had in the Court from which the case is transferred, not on evidence
already recorded by any Court or Special Judge or his predecessors in Office.
(B) Save as
provided in sub-section (1), the provisions of the said Code, except the provisions
of section 196A and of Chapter XXXIII, shall, so far as they are not
inconsistent with this Act, apply to all proceedings of a Special Judge, and
for the purposes of the said provisions the Special Judges, shall be deemed to
be a Court of Session trying cases without a jury, and a person conducting a
prosecution before a Special Judge shall be deemed to be a Public Prosecutor.

Appeal and revision

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
17. Appeal and revision.--The High Court may exercise so far as
they may be applicable, all the powers conferred by Chapters XXXII and XXXIII
of the Code of Criminal Procedure V of 1898 on a High Court, as if the Special
Judge were a Court of Session trying cases without a jury within the local
limits of the High Court's jurisdiction.

Bar of certain jurisdictions

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
18. Bar of certain jurisdictions.--No Court other than a High Court
shall have authority to transfer any case from a Special Judge to any other
Court of Special Judge or to make any order under section 491 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure V of 1898, or save as provided in section 17, have any
jurisdiction of any kind in respect of any proceedings of a Special Judge.

Burden of proof in certain cases

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
19. Burden of proof in certain cases.--When any person is tried for
an offence of hoarding or dealing in the black market and any question arises
whether he did any act or was in possession of anything with lawful authority
or under a permit, licence or other document
prescribed by or such authority, permit, licence or
other document shall lie on him.

Accused person to be competent witness

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
20. Accused person to be competent witness.--Notwithstanding
anything to the contrary in any enactment for the time being in force, any
person charged with hoarding or dealing in the black market shall be a
competent witness in his own defence, and may give
evidence on oath in disproof of the charges made against him or against any
person charged together with him at the same trial.
Provided that:‑
(a) he shall not be called as a witness except at his own
request;
(b) his failure
to give evidence shall not be made the subject of any comment by the prosecution
or give rise to any presumption against him or against any person charged
together with him at the sum trial;
(c) he shall not be asked any question tending to show that he
has committed or been convicted or any offence other than the offence with
which he is charged, or is of bad character, unless--
(i) the proof that he has committed
or been convicted of such offence is admissible evidence to show that he is
guilty of the offence with which he is charged, or
(ii) he has
personally or by his pleader asked questions of any witness for the prosecution
with a view to establishing his own good character, or has given evidence of
his good character, or;
(iii) he has given evidence in disproof of the charges made
against any other person charged together with him at the same trial.

Notice of conviction to be displayed

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
21. Notice of conviction to be displayed.--(1) Upon the conviction
of any person for the offence of hoarding in the or dealing in the black
market, as the case may be, the Government may require him to exhibit in or
outside or both in and outside his place of business (if any) notices of such
particulars relating to the conviction as it may determine and to keep them so
exhibit continuously for a period of not less than three months from date of
conviction; and if he fails to comply fully with the requirement he shall be
deemed to have committed a further offence of hoarding or dealing in the black
market, as the case may be, according to the nature of the original offence for
which he was convicted.
If any person so convicted
refuses or fails to comply fully with any such requirement, may officer authorised in that behalf by an order of the Government in
writing may, without prejudice to any proceedings which may be brought in
respect of any such refusal or failure, affix the notice in or outside, or both
in and outside, the place of business of such person in accordance with the
requirement of the Government in pursuance of the last proceeding sub-section.
(3) Any person who obstructs any
such officer in exercise of any power conferred by sub section (2) shall be
punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend
to two years or with fine or with both.
(4) If in any case the Government
is satisfied that the exhibition of notices in accordance with the requirements
of the foregoing provisions of this section will not effectively bring the
conviction to the notice of persons dealing with the convicted person, the
Government may, in lieu of or in addition to any such requirement, require the
convicted person to exhibit for such period, not being a period of less than
three months, on such stationery used in his business as may be specified in the
requirement a notice placed in such position and printed in type of such size
and found and containing such particulars relating to the conviction as may be
specified in the requirement, and if he fails to comply fully with the
requirement he shall be deemed to have committed a further offence of hoarding
or dealing in the black market, as the case may be, according to the nature of
the original offence for which he was convicted.
sections.punishment:
punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend
to two years or with fine or with both.

sections.description:
Powers to publish conviction

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
22. Powers to publish conviction.--If the Government is satisfied
that it is necessary so to do, the conviction and the particulars relating to
the conviction of any person for an offence under this Act may be published in
the Official Gazette.

Indemnity

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
23. Indemnity.--No suit, prosecution or legal proceeding whatever
shall lie against any public servant in respect of anything which is in good faith
done or intended to be done under this Act.

Except as otherwise provided in this Act

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
24. Except as otherwise provided in this Act,
imprisonment for any offence under this Act shall be rigorous.

Rule making powers

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ACT, 1948
(ACT XXIX OF 1948)
An Act to make special provision for checking hoarding and dealing in
the black market
25. Rule making powers.--The Central Government may make rules for
carrying out the purposes of this Act.
